1
Project Detail → Team Tab

Phase Schedule — Dual Views

Two purpose-built perspectives for the same team data — a rich schedule chart for analysis, and a fast card list for editing allocation hours.

Schedule View
Cumulative progress chart — S-curve plotting total hours burned week by week. Tooltip shows week date, hours that week, and cumulative % complete per phase.
Phase-scoped team grid — every member's EAC hours, ETC cost, and per-week hours column, scoped to the selected phase.
Weekly team total row — bottom aggregate row reveals peak-load weeks instantly.
Progress metadata — % complete, total / spent / remaining hours, and date range per phase card.
Schedule View — cumulative hours chart, phase team breakdown, EAC/ETC per member
Team List View — Schedule Hours Popup (3 Modes)
⚡
Uniform Weekly Hours
Enter one hours/week value — it's applied to every week of the assignment at once. Fastest way to set a flat rate across the full timeline.
📅
Set Hours for a Date Range
Pick From–To dates, set hours/week, then add more rows with + for different periods. Ideal for ramp-up or ramp-down across phases.
⚖️
Distribute Evenly
Spreads total allocated hours evenly across all weeks — e.g. 3,200h ÷ 135 weeks = 24h/week, calculated and applied automatically.
Team List — allocation cards with heat-bar timeline per member
Schedule Hours popup — three allocation entry modes
2
Pipeline → Project Card

Conflict Detection + AI Analysis

Shared team members who are simultaneously assigned across multiple projects are surfaced on the project card — and AI delivers specific reallocation guidance on click.

Project card — shared member conflict and overlap % shown on expand
Collapsed card indicator — an amber "X shared members · Y% team overlap" chip appears on the card surface without expanding it.
Expanded conflict detail — shows which members are shared, their allocation % on this project vs. the other, and hours booked on each.
AI Conflict Analysis on click — identifies the over-allocation, labels severity (OVER-ALLOCATED), explains the delivery risk, and provides ranked, specific recommendations.
Next Action — always surfaces one decisive step so the PM has an immediate, clear path forward (not just a diagnosis).
Example AI output: "Reduce Downtown Rail Extension — Phase 2 from 90% to 70%." and "Increase Harbor Waterfront Mixed-Use Tower from 30% to 50%." — specific numbers, not generic advice.
AI Conflict Analysis — allocation breakdown, risk, ranked recommendations, and Next Action
3
Pipeline → Companies Tab

Companies — Redesigned UI

The Companies tab is rebuilt as a card-first layout with a pipeline distribution bar, per-client metrics, and full click-through navigation.

Pipeline distribution bar — colour-coded horizontal bar showing each client's share of total pipeline value with a live legend.
Client cards with live metrics — initials logo, project count, pipeline value (colour-coded by client), and Open / Active / Closed breakdown.
Quick filter tabs — toggle between Projects, Opps, and Leads within each company without leaving the Companies view.
Clickable cards — every company card navigates into that client's full record with associated pipeline items.
Instant search — filters the card grid by client name in real time.
Companies — card grid, distribution bar, and per-client Open / Active / Closed counts
4
Resources → Timeline Tab

Timeline — Fully Interactive + Gantt

Every element of the Timeline is now clickable — week dates, utilisation bars, hour counts, project names — all opening contextual drill-down panels. Plus a dedicated Gantt view.

Resources Timeline — weekly utilisation grid, Grid / Gantt / Weekly / Monthly toggles, and Project filter pill
Week-date headers clickable — clicking a column header (6/29, 7/6…) opens a week-level summary: all active resources, hours, utilisation %, and Overloaded / Good status.
Utilisation bars clickable — opens that person's individual resource profile for the week — hours booked, utilisation %, active projects, and a timeline chart across all periods.
Project names clickable — project links inside any drill-down navigate directly to the project detail page.
AI Analysis per person — AI ANALYSIS link on each project allocation row, plus a "Full AI Analysis" button for a comprehensive workload review.
Gantt chart mode — switching to Gantt shows a timeline-based allocation picture across all resources instead of the weekly bar grid.
Week popup — all resources, hours, utilisation %, and status for the selected week
Person drill-down — resource timeline chart, active projects, and AI Analysis link
5
Resources → Staff & Timeline

Project Filter — Staff & Timeline

A new Project filter pill sits alongside BU, Division, Department, Role, and Job Title on both the Staff and Timeline tabs — scope any view to a specific project in one click.

Staff tab — Project filter dropdown; filter pills cascade: BU · Division · Role · Job Title · Project
Project pill filter — "Project ↓" dropdown lists all active projects. Selecting one narrows the staff list and timeline grid to only members allocated to that project.
Cascading with other filters — stacks with BU, Division, Department, Role, and Job Title. E.g. show only Architects in the Architecture BU on a specific project.
On both tabs — identical filter available on Resources → Staff and Resources → Timeline for a consistent experience.
6
Resources → Staff

Concentration Risk

When a staff member allocates more than a configurable threshold of their time to a single project, an automatic flag prevents unnoticed over-reliance on one person per engagement.

Automatic amber chip — "Concentration risk" appears on the staff card surface alongside overload indicators when the threshold is breached.
Visible without expanding — PMs spot the risk at a glance without having to open each individual profile.
AI Analysis clickable — clicking the chip opens an AI panel that identifies which project causes the concentration and recommends diversification actions.
Threshold configurable — set in Settings → Staff → D) Concentration risk threshold (%). Default: 80%.
Settings: Settings → Staff → D) Concentration risk threshold (%). If a person spends more than this % on one project, the flag activates across all staff views.
Staff card (expanded) — Concentration risk chip, overallocation detail, active projects, org & employment
AI Analysis — CRITICAL: 190% concentration on one project · ranked actions to diversify immediately
7
Resources → Staff → Profile

Skills, Experience Tags & Resume Download

Every staff profile now stores Skills and Experience Tags. One click generates and downloads a professionally formatted PDF resume populated with live allocation and org data.

Skills tags — editable chips per person (e.g. SketchUp, BIM, AutoCAD, Rhino). Edited inline with a dedicated Edit button.
Experience Tags — separate tag set for project-type or sector experience (e.g. Education, Mixed-Use, Residential). Used for filtering and AI matching.
Download Resume — one-click PDF generation from the Resource Profile modal. The PDF includes name / title / email, Current Role table, Current Allocations with gauge and project table, and Skills bars.
Assign to Project via AI — the profile modal also offers AI-guided project assignment directly from the profile view.
Resource Profile — Download Resume, AI assign, 190% load gauge, and org/employment table
Generated PDF — role table, allocations with gauge, project table, and skills bars. RM ONE branded.
8
Resources → Demand Tab

Demand — URGENT Flag & AI Analysis

Unfilled demand roles starting within your urgency window are automatically tagged URGENT — with a full AI analysis panel that drives immediate, prioritised action.

URGENT demand panel — AI narrative, allocation detail, and four prioritised recommended actions
Demand cards — URGENT tag on each card, 125% hard allocation gauge, Find Staff AI button, and View Details per open role week
URGENT tag — any unfilled role starting within the urgency window shows a bold red URGENT label on its demand card. Roles past their start date are always urgent.
AI Analysis on click — opens a panel with role/project/days-until-start, current allocation state, a plain-language risk summary, and ranked recommended actions.
Four recommended actions — (1) Scan Staff for available capacity, (2) Find Staff AI matching, (3) Open external posting in parallel, (4) Review project timeline for contingency start date.
Urgency window configurable — set in Settings → Staff → F) Demand urgency window (days). Default: 400 days.
Settings link: Settings → Staff → F) Demand urgency window (days). Roles within this window — or already past start date — always show URGENT on Resources → Demand.
Demand cards — every unfilled role shows URGENT tag, 125% hard allocation gauge, View Details and Find Staff AI buttons
9
Forecast Page

Forecast — Targets, Financials, Filters & Win Pursuit

Pipeline coverage tracking against a configurable target, BU/Division filtering, live financial headlines, and "what if we win this?" scenario modelling — all on one page.

Forecast — peak overload week, hiring trigger, resource failure point, and Win Pursuit scenario selector
Pipeline coverage target — a % target (e.g. 116%) set in Settings is tracked live. The page header shows gap/surplus and surfaces when demand will cross capacity.
Financial headlines — peak overload week, hiring trigger month (with role), and resource failure point — all derived from live weekly demand vs. capacity.
BU and Division filter — scope the entire forecast to one Business Unit or Division so segment heads see only their capacity picture.
Win Pursuit scenario — select any open opportunity and click "Win pursuit" to instantly re-run the forecast with that project included — showing updated FTE impact and hiring trigger shift.
Switch pursuit project — swap between different open opportunities from the dropdown and compare forecast outcomes side-by-side before committing.
Settings: E) Forecast window (weeks) — how far ahead the analysis runs. G) Pipeline coverage target (%) — what counts as a healthy pipeline. Both shown on the Forecast page as live benchmarks.
10
Organization Page

Organization Tier Pipeline — Toggle BU & Department

Many firms don't use all three org tiers. Toggle Business Unit and Department on or off — the entire application adapts: forms, filter bars, and reports update instantly with no re-import required.

Organization — three-tier toggle panel and live visual hierarchy (BU → Division → Department → Job Title)
Three-tier toggle panel — Tier 1 (Business Unit) and Tier 3 (Department) each have an on/off toggle. Tier 2 (Division) is always on — it is the core billing and assignment unit.
App-wide data pipeline — toggling a tier removes it from all create/edit forms, filter bars (Staff, Timeline, Forecast), and every report or card that references it.
Live visual org tree — colour-coded tree diagram of your full hierarchy (BU → Division → Department → Job Title) renders below the toggles.
Template & Upload — bulk-import org structure from Excel using the Download Template and Upload buttons.
Impact: Turning off Tier 1 (Business Unit) removes BU from every form and filter across the entire app. Tier 2 (Division) is always on — core of assignments and billing.
11–13
Settings Page

Schedule, Staff & Forecast Settings

Granular controls that propagate automatically to all existing allocations, staff views, and the forecast — no manual recalculation required.

11 Schedule Settings
Controls how far back users can edit hours, which days are working days, and the standard hours in a full week.
A — Hours Grid
Allow Editing Past Weeks
Toggle past-week editing. Choose how far back: 1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 26, 52 weeks, Unlimited, or a Custom number. Locks past cells to prevent accidental back-dated changes.
B — Non-Working Days
Non-Working Days
Select which weekdays are non-working (e.g. Sat + Sun). Selected days appear as dots in column headers and are marked OFF in the week-detail popup. Applied to all existing allocations automatically.
Schedule Settings — past-week editing range selector and non-working day picker (Sat + Sun shown off)
C — Hours in a Full Week: Setting this (e.g. 40h) defines 100% capacity. Changing it re-derives all existing allocation percentages automatically across all schedule and resource views.
12 Staff Settings
Five knobs control allocation colour-coding and when demand is treated as urgent.
A — Over-capacity
Over-Capacity Flag (%)
Above this %, person flagged red (over-allocated) on Resources → Staff and Timeline. Default: 110%.
B — Optimal band
Optimal Band Start (%)
Where the green Optimal band begins. Also sets the home health score target. Default: 80%.
C — Under-allocated
Under-Allocated Flag (%)
At or below this (and above 0%), person flagged amber. Default: 60%.
D — Conc. risk
Concentration Risk (%)
If a person spends more than this % on one project, the Concentration risk chip activates on their staff card. Default: 80%.
Staff Settings — A–C utilisation thresholds, D) concentration risk %, F) demand urgency window (days)
F — Demand Urgency Window (days): Unfilled demand roles starting within this many days show URGENT on Resources → Demand. Default: 400 days. Past-start-date roles are always urgent.
13 Forecast Settings
Two settings that define the Forecast page's scope and success benchmark.
E — Forecast window
Forecast Look-Ahead (weeks)
How many weeks ahead the Forecast page analyses demand vs. capacity. Increasing this surfaces hiring triggers further in advance. Default: 8 weeks.
G — Pipeline target
Pipeline Coverage Target (%)
Healthy pipeline = at least this % of active project portfolio value. Tracked live on the Forecast page. Default: 116%.
Forecast Settings — E) forecast window (weeks), G) pipeline coverage target (%)
